newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Chamber of Commerce criticizes Fed rate hike.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Chamber of Commerce criticizes Fed rate hike.

text.p: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce on Tuesday criticized the Federal Reserve's decision to raise interest rates for the first time in over two years.
"With no inflation in the current data, and few, if any signs of future inflation, we believe the Fed had room to wait," Chamber chief economist Martin Regalia said in a statement.
"Clearly the pressure to raise rates came from the brokerage houses on Wall Street, not the small businesses on Main Street," Regalia added.
The business group said that since the financial markets have already raised rates in anticipation of the Fed's move, its action will have only a modest impact on economic activty.
"However, if this is merely a first step in a replay of 1994, economic growth will be noticeably impacted," the Chamber said.

The Fed raised the federal funds rate that commercial banks charge each other for overnight loans by one-quarter of a percentage point to 5.50 percent. The Fed left the discount rate it charges banks for money unchanged at 5.0 percent.
